summary: The proposal supplies a coherent read-only architecture, conservative publication observation, explicit resource ceilings, separate List state, and credible distribution boundaries. Four contract ambiguities must be resolved before independent consumers implement it: exact query binding, complete wire definitions, progress past oversized items, and runtime helper-version changes. No rejection is based on later browser, performance, installation, or human-validation work being unperformed.

mandatory_defects.title: Bind continuation to the exact query semantics, not only casefolded normalization
candidate_evidence: ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:162 says scope contains the normalized query.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:190 hashes normalized selectors without defining an exact trimmed query component.
governing_evidence: SKILLS-depo/ontology/scripts/ontology_retrieval.py:25-36: normalize casefolds and collapses whitespace, whereas query_text only strips outer whitespace.

SKILLS-depo/ontology/scripts/ontology_retrieval.py:29-30,39-64: exact-ID equality uses the original query and lexical tokenization splits CamelCase before casefolding; ranked results therefore depend on distinctions discarded by normalize().
TRD REQ-005 retains canonical ranking, and REQ-024 requires a changed query to begin a new sequence.
mandatory_defects.failure_case: TaskManager and taskmanager have the same normalize() result but different lexical token sets. Likewise a case-changed canonical ID loses exact-ID precedence. A cursor keyed only by normalize() may validate against a different ranking and apply the old last_key, skipping or duplicating results. The current wording permits that implementation.
mandatory_defects.correction: Define the exact search query identity as canonical query_text(query), preserving case and interior characters, with an explicit separate empty-browse representation. Bind that exact value or its digest into the cursor scope and client response-acceptance key. Keep any casefolded value as an additional display/search component, not the sole identity. Specify the nonempty sort behavior consistently with canonical relevance ranking. Add contract examples requiring a new sequence or cursor_scope_changed for TaskManager/taskmanager and case-changed stable IDs; trimming equivalence may remain explicit.

mandatory_defects.title: Finish the exact operation and error wire definitions before consumer implementation
candidate_evidence: ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:138-143 lists the six requests but describes several response data objects only by meaning.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:148-159 still uses scope:{...validated normalized operation scope...} and data:{...operation data...}.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:168-173 groups several HTTP statuses with several codes without a one-to-one mapping.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:180-184 mentions section chunks and omitted-item metadata but gives no enclosing entry/source/omitted-item response shape.
governing_evidence: CONTRACTS baseline criterion 1 requires exact request/envelope/error/cursor shapes.
manager/contracts-review-checklist.md requires exact response envelopes, code/status agreement, field types and text/ID caps.
TRD REQ-023 requires validated operation responses with explicit scope, coverage, limits, continuation and distinguishable safe failures.
mandatory_defects.failure_case: Independent server and frontend implementers must choose field names and nesting for context capabilities, entry sections, source content/observations, omitted relationships, and allowed source_state values. They must also choose which status resource_limit uses and what request_id/operation contain when a malformed unauthenticated request cannot supply them. Those choices cannot yet be mechanically checked for agreement from this proposal.
mandatory_defects.correction: Supply closed per-operation data and scope schemas, including nullability, enums, required/optional keys, exact section/source/omitted-item nesting and allowed ID/string limits. Give each error code exactly one HTTP status, safe message class and retry enum, including malformed pre-auth request metadata. Define explicit lower bounds/types for the lowerable configuration keys and the resulting effective-limits response. A compact normative schema/table is sufficient; product code or completed runtime tests are not required for this revision.

mandatory_defects.title: Define forward progress when one result cannot fit the response budget
candidate_evidence: ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:182 requires omitting an edge whose complete qualifiers cannot fit, while retaining its exact ID.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:184 says not to advance continuation beyond a removed item, then permits a bounded omitted-item record for a single oversized item.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:190 defines last_key as the last returned ranking key or relation ID without saying whether an omitted marker consumes that key.
governing_evidence: TRD REQ-018 requires honest bounded degradation plus narrowing/continuation.
TRD REQ-024 and AT-05 require stable bounded continuation without skipped or duplicate identities.
The CONTRACTS checklist explicitly requires continuation semantics and honest coverage.
mandatory_defects.failure_case: If the next qualifying relation has qualifiers larger than the full configured envelope, repeating the same cursor can keep returning the same omitted marker while the 'do not advance' rule prevents reaching later small relations. Advancing without a defined consumed marker instead risks silently skipping the oversized relation. The two policies are not reconciled.
mandatory_defects.correction: Distinguish a temporarily byte-deferred item from a permanently unrenderable item. Define a typed omitted/detail marker that consumes exactly that stable key, counts under an explicit page rule, remains visibly incomplete and offers lossless entry-section access; allow next_cursor to advance past that returned marker. Alternatively define an explicit bounded alternate continuation operation with equivalent no-silent-loss semantics. Specify examples with an oversized first/middle item followed by fitting items and the case where even a marker cannot fit.

mandatory_defects.title: Bind snapshot helper identity to the code actually loaded by the service
candidate_evidence: ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:47 starts one Python worker from fixed installed scripts at service startup.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:122-126 includes exact helper/adapter digests in snapshots and says helper changes create a new validated candidate snapshot.
ART_CONTRACTS_DATA_V1.md:224-226 permits an existing client to refresh atomically to a newly accepted snapshot.
governing_evidence: SKILLS-depo/ontology/scripts/ontology_core.py:388-389 hashes current on-disk ontology*.py files when materializing a snapshot; it does not reload executing modules.
TRD REQ-021 requires one coherent selected-input version and REQ-022 explicitly keys caches by helper/adapter version.
mandatory_defects.failure_case: Replacing a loaded helper or adapter file during service life changes disk hashes while Python continues executing its already imported code. Rematerializing under the newly observed digests can claim new helper semantics while executing old semantics; an already loaded frontend can likewise retain a different contract/build epoch. Digest-before/after equality alone does not solve loaded-code identity.
mandatory_defects.correction: Pin the executing helper/adapter/schema/build closure at startup and define code-epoch drift separately from reloadable ontology/presentation data. The simplest rule is fail closed with a documented reopen/package-changed error when any executing-code or wire-schema/build member changes, preserve the old visible context, and require a fresh verified service/client session before accepting new reads. A supervised full worker restart is another option only if it verifies the complete new closure and explicitly invalidates affected sessions/cursors/client contract state. State that no new snapshot may advertise helper hashes that do not identify its executing code.
